meta.title: Career — Nagy Habib
meta.description: From Ain Shams, Edinburgh and Bristol, and training with Henri Bismuth and Thomas Starzl, to Imperial College London since 2003: the career of Professor Nagy Habib.

sections.label: Career
sections.sub: Ain Shams, Edinburgh and Bristol; training with Henri Bismuth and Thomas Starzl; then four decades of surgery, research and invention, at Imperial College London since 2003.

sections.label: Imperial College London
sections.title: Surgeon, professor, <t>Pro-Rector.</t>
sections.lede: Roles as listed by Imperial College London and in his own signature.

groups.label: Roles
names: Professor of Hepatobiliary Surgery, Department of Surgery & Cancer, Faculty of Medicine — since 1 June 2003
Academic Head of HPB Surgery, Imperial College London
Pro-Rector for Commercial Affairs and member of the College Management Board — from June 2007
Centre for Advanced Therapeutics, Imperial College London

groups.label: In the theatre
names: Liver, pancreas and biliary surgery at Hammersmith Hospital
Radiofrequency-assisted, near-bloodless liver resection
First living-related liver transplant in Africa and the Middle East, 1993

groups.label: In the laboratory
names: First clinical trial of adenovirus and plasmid gene therapy for liver cancer; plasmid gene therapy by hydrodynamic delivery
First in the West to publish a clinical trial of autologous adult bone-marrow stem cells for liver insufficiency
Small activating RNA: from the preclinical work to the first-in-human trial of MTL-CEBPA, 2020

marks.t: First living-related liver transplant in Africa

groups.label: Academic & clinical
names: Academic Head of HPB Surgery, Imperial College London
Hepatopancreatobiliary surgery, Hammersmith Hospital

groups.label: Committees & boards
names: Member, Académie Nationale de Chirurgie, France
Member, Research & Funding Sub-Committee, Royal College of Surgeons of Edinburgh — 2026 to 2028
Member, Advisory Committee on Clinical Impact Awards (ACCIA)
Charity Board Trustee, MPS Society (mucopolysaccharidosis diseases), UK — since 2026
Scientific Advisory Board, MiNA Therapeutics

groups.label: Honorary
names: Honorary professorships in Egypt, China, Romania and Greece

groups.label: Degrees and fellowships
names: ChM, University of Bristol
FRCS, Royal College of Surgeons of Edinburgh — 1981
MBBCh, Ain Shams University, Cairo — 1972 to 1977

groups.label: Training
names: With Professor Henri Bismuth and Professor Thomas Starzl
Arabic, French and English, at full professional level

sections.d: Selected papers, a book and lectures.
